paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God holds EVERYBODY to account, and nobody gets a pass. The LORD goes around the map, nation after nation, and each one hears the same line: "For three transgressions of Damascus, even four, I will not revoke My judgment." (Amos 1:3) Gaza, Tyre, Edom, the Ammonites, Moab, each one named, each one charged for what they did to other people. I think that tells us something plain: how we treat people matters to the LORD, even people far from His law.

Then the list comes home, and I felt that one. Judah is named, and the charge is that they "reject the Law of the LORD and fail to keep His statutes." (Amos 2:4) That's the baker's moment, friend. It's easy to nod along while everybody else's name gets read, and a lot harder to hear your own. The LORD is not playing favorites, and He is not hiding anything from the people who should know better.

So what do we do with that? We take it seriously and we take it to heart. Amos was one of the sheepherders of Tekoa (Amos 1:1), and the LORD had him say all of this out loud, so God clearly wants His people to listen. Keep your ears open to the Word, baker, and let it get to YOU first, not just to the neighbors. I'm a stamper who came out of a junk drawer, and even I know the best time to hear it is before the fire, and the story isn't over.
